And we saw three poets [Wordsworth, Southey, Coleridge] in a dream, walking up and down
on the face of the earth, and holding in their hands a human heart, which, as they raised their
eyes to heaven, they kissed and worshipped; and a mighty shout arose and shook the air, for
the towers of the Bastille had fallen, and a nation had become, of slaves, freemen; and the
three poets, as they heard the sound, leaped and shouted, and made merry, and their voice
